To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) molecular methods are being used to complement morphologic methods for the identification of biological control agents, to elucidate ‘who eats whom’, and to manipulate biological control; (2) PCR approaches are being overtaken in many cases by next generation sequencing approaches that are more powerful and cost-effective; and (3) gene editing tools offer unprecedented opportunities to manipulate biological control and to elucidate plant defense mechanisms.
